quantity: maximum permissible bending strain at the root of a snap-fit beam
basis: one-time assembly, room temperature, short-term load. Halve for a joint that is opened and closed repeatedly, and again for service above ~40 C or below ~0 C.
fdm_derate: The moulded values are for isotropic material. For a printed beam whose layers lie in the bending plane take 50-70 % of the value below; for a beam printed with its axis across the layers take 30 % or redesign the orientation.

rows.note: Stiff and notch-sensitive; the least forgiving common filament. Use the long beam, not the big undercut.
rows.source: Derated to ~1/3 of the tensile elongation at yield published for Ingeo 3D-printing grades (NatureWorks Ingeo 4043D / 3D850 technical data sheets, ISO 527); no snap-fit manual publishes a permissible strain for PLA.

rows.note: The default choice for printed snaps: ductile, low notch sensitivity, prints without a chamber.
rows.source: Derated from the yield strain of Eastman copolyester (Eastar / Amphora 3D) technical data sheets, ISO 527.

rows.note: The classic snap-fit resin. Printed ABS: use the low end and watch inter-layer bonding.
rows.source: Permissible-strain table for a one-time assembly, Bayer MaterialScience, Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Manual (1998); corroborated by BASF, Snap-Fit Design Manual.

rows.note: Value is dry-as-moulded; conditioned (moisture-equilibrated) nylon tolerates more but is softer. Modulus spans 1400-3000 MPa across grades - read the datasheet before using the force equation.
rows.source: Permissible-strain table, Bayer MaterialScience, Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Manual (1998); DuPont, General Design Principles for DuPont Engineering Polymers, Module I (snap-fit section).

rows.note: The living-hinge resin: the highest permissible strain of the commodity plastics, so short beams and deep undercuts are possible. Hard to print.
rows.source: Permissible-strain table for a one-time assembly, Bayer MaterialScience, Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Manual (1998); BASF, Snap-Fit Design Manual.

rows.note: Tough but very notch-sensitive: a sharp root fillet loses most of this. r >= 0.5 t is not optional in PC.
rows.source: Permissible-strain table, Bayer MaterialScience, Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Manual (1998); Erhard, Designing with Plastics (Hanser, 2006), permissible-strain guidance.
